steps.content: Levy, you've gone too far!

steps.speaker: Levy
steps.content: That'll be 73,500,200 DisCoins. Since we're relatives, keep the two hundred. But that private sand boat you've just bought will be mine. Be sure to clean up the trash on the boat. I'm kind of a neat freak, you know.
Levy, you! I...
We're... family, after all, how could you...

steps.speaker: Levy
steps.content: Crying won't get you anything, dear cousin. Grow up. This is a board meeting with so many people watching. Aren't you ashamed?

steps.speaker: Levy
steps.content: Hey, don't rub it with your dirty hands. Two hundred DisCoins are not enough to pay for pink eye treatment.

steps.speaker: Levy
steps.content: And don't give me that kicked-puppy look. You've gotta get me that money even if it means pawning your last pair of pants...
Shut up! I won't let you humiliate my father any more!

steps.speaker: Levy
steps.content: Oh, don't you worry, Chaddy. I won't make you pay your father's debt. If he dies, I'll be your guardian. I must do my part for the family, mustn't I?

steps.speaker: Levy
steps.content: Aaahhh!
In the interrogation room, Levy swings his arm in a cast nonchalantly.
You should avoid moving it if you want it to heal soon.

steps.speaker: Levy
steps.content: Relax. Back in the day, I once broke my leg in a fight and went clubbing as soon as I got the cast. It healed just fine after.

steps.speaker: Levy
steps.content: Hehe, speaking of which, why do you care so much about me?

steps.speaker: Levy
steps.content: Curious? About what?
About how an ordinary boy could crack the metacarpal bone of a Sinner with Endura Tendency...

steps.speaker: Levy
steps.content: Nonsense. How could he hurt me? I fell on my own!

steps.speaker: Levy
steps.content: I slipped and fell, knocking my hand on the step. It has nothing to do with that boy.
Then why did you ask to see him after that fall cracked your metacarpal bone?

steps.speaker: Levy
steps.content: It's only natural that an uncle would want to see his nephew who's strayed into questionable territory. Or do you think I'd seek revenge on a kid?
Based on what I know of you...
Yes.

steps.speaker: Levy
steps.content: ...You're right. I'm going to sell Chaddy to a private Hypercube mine as a coolie to cover my medical expenses...
Levy said that menacingly. When he saw your icy expression, he began to explain gleefully.

steps.speaker: Levy
steps.content: Tsk, look at you. I'm joking! Have you got no sense of humor?

steps.speaker: Levy
steps.content: And why does it look like you're interrogating me? Shouldn't you be questioning Chad instead? I'm the victim!
Levy pointed at his injured arm a little indignantly. He's obviously a little careless with his movement, as it seemed to tug at his wound.

steps.speaker: Levy
steps.content: Ouch...
After his brief "performance", he noticed your indifference to his exaggerated acting and decided to initiate small talk.

steps.speaker: Levy
steps.content: By the way, Chief, do you know what's the best part of getting wrapped in bandages?
What?

steps.speaker: Levy
steps.content: Look, the nurses wrote their good wishes on it. Things like get well soon, speedy recovery, etc.
Levy raises his bandaged arm.
Not everyone gets this kind of privilege.

steps.speaker: Levy
steps.content: I know, I know. I'm hot and loaded, after all. It's normal the nurses are being particularly nice to me.

steps.speaker: Levy
steps.content: But it's not like these words can actually help my injury heal faster. If I were a little more antisocial, I would even think they were being annoying.
What are you trying to say?

steps.speaker: Levy
steps.content: Nothing. I just think people are obsessed with seemingly useful but practically meaningless things.
What's meaningful to you then? Taking revenge on your nephew?
Levy raised an eyebrow.

steps.speaker: Levy
steps.content: Please, I thought we were over that? Besides, what can I gain from being petty with a child... You, on the other hand.

steps.speaker: Levy
steps.content: Sitting here and interrogating me. It doesn't get more meaningless than that.
He leans over from the chair, looking you up and down like examining a product.

steps.speaker: Levy
steps.content: Hmm, well, I guess that's quite an achievement, at least.

steps.speaker: Levy
steps.content: Hey, why don't you tell me how it feels like to sit there?

steps.speaker: Levy
steps.content: When you sit in that chair, the Sinners must tell you whatever you want them to tell. You've got the MBCC and even the entire government behind you, and the infallible shackles.

steps.speaker: Levy
steps.content: It must feel amazing. Power is the most luxurious addiction, you see.

steps.speaker: Levy
steps.content: Be careful though. Not every Sinner is harmless like me. You're very powerful, but even someone like you can't watch their back all the time.

steps.speaker: Levy
steps.content: If you run into a murderous psycho one day, no power or special ability can save your ass.
The mockery in Levy's words is blatant. But you know a thing or two about dealing with people like him.

options: Ignore the mockery and take back control

choices.text: Ignore the mockery and take back control

steps.content: Be direct, Levy. I know full well what power my position grants me, and I accept the risks and the price that come with it.
But you... I can tell you don't like to be here, do you? Cooperate with me and help me understand the cause and consequence of the incident, then I'll let you go.

steps.speaker: Levy
steps.content: Haha, interesting...

steps.speaker: Levy
steps.content: You hate me, but you tell yourself: he's a Sinner. He might be useful some day.

steps.speaker: Levy
steps.content: That's exhausting. If someone disgusts you, you should simply punch them in the face like my little nephew did.
You didn't respond to his provocation but produced the evidence instead.

This is Chad, right? The one who hit you.

steps.speaker: Levy
steps.content: I told you, he didn't do it. I fell on my own.
Levy grumbled as he took a glance at the photo, then at you.

steps.speaker: Levy
steps.content: Sigh, I was shocked too. Didn't think that kid would really dare to do it.
What do you mean?

steps.speaker: Levy
steps.content: I mean, Chad is the son of my cousin. I watched him grow up. Growing up, he's always followed me around, calling me Uncle Levy.

steps.speaker: Levy
steps.content: I was heartbroken that this should have happened.
If you were that close, why would he attack you?
Levy frowned.

steps.speaker: Levy
steps.content: Because of... a minor dispute over some property.
Minor dispute?
Did you know that after the Public Security Bureau arrived and subdued Chad, they found a gun on him?
Had he been a little more reckless, it wouldn't have been just a fistfight. He would have shot you.

steps.speaker: Levy
steps.content: Nonsense. Chad has always been a decent kid. How would he possibly want to shoot me?
Levy looks taken aback. Apparently, he was unaware of this.
Then why did he carry a gun to the board meeting?
I'm afraid this is no minor dispute.

The document says that the two parties have been disputing over property worth dozens of million DisCoins recently. But for a family of wealthy entrepreneurs in Eastside, it doesn't sound like that much of a big deal.
Your cousin didn't file for bankruptcy protection?

steps.speaker: Levy
steps.content: Bankruptcy, huh? He just bought a villa with three balconies, a private pool, and a central thermostat. You can't imagine how cozy that house is. Even I'm getting envious... Ugh, I digress.
Levy looks like he's holding back something. He must be hiding some secret.
After a slightly dramatic sigh, Levy finally begins.

steps.speaker: Levy
steps.content: Frankly, I know Chad too well. That boy is always broody and alarmingly quiet. He's a good kid.

steps.speaker: Levy
steps.content: Even if puberty screwed up part of his brain, I bet he wouldn't come up with the idea of carrying a gun.
So you're saying someone put him up to it?

steps.speaker: Levy
steps.content: Do I have to spell it out? You don't know my cousin. The fourth shareholder of Fort Limited with two companies and a large assembly plant under his name. Sounds like a respectable fella, yeah?

steps.speaker: Levy
steps.content: Tsk, in reality, being a respectable fella means "acting respectable and leaving all the dirty deeds to others."

steps.speaker: Levy
steps.content: He won't even hesitate to use his own son. He feels no such thing as guilt.
You mean your cousin is the true culprit?

steps.speaker: Levy
steps.content: Hey, don't give me that doubtful look.

steps.speaker: Levy
steps.content: At first, I thought Chad hit me because he didn't like the way I talked to his dad, but I didn't know about the gun... What a shame, I've always spoiled that kid.
Hey, that's a little too much, drama queen.

steps.speaker: Levy
steps.content: If you can't tell how heartbroken I am, then at least look at my arm. Do you know how hard it's been to relieve myself in the past few days?
Levy swung his injured arm once again.
I've been shot by a gun before. No need to remind me of how it feels.

steps.speaker: Levy
steps.content: But Chad, my little nephew, he suffers worse pain. He has such a kind heart, but now he's been misled by his dad and his gang of so-called friends.

steps.speaker: Levy
steps.content: At first, I thought it was fine even if you wouldn't let me see him. A few days in the cell will help calm him down. At least he'll know he shouldn't act on impulse again.

steps.speaker: Levy
steps.content: But I swear I didn't know about this. Now if I don't go and have a chat with him, he may really cross into criminal territory.
It's very hard not to take your eagerness to see your nephew as a potential plan of revenge.
Or, as you've said, perhaps you want to use Chad to take revenge on his father.

steps.speaker: Levy
steps.content: But he's my family! Do you really not trust me?
I've looked into your background, which has led me to believe that you don't deserve my trust.
The people in your family took over your deceased parents' property when you were a teenager. But in just a few years, your family all either fled or died. Things didn't end up well for them.
Claiming someone is your family doesn't sound reassuring at all.

steps.speaker: Levy
steps.content: That hurts... And you can't be saying these things without proof. Rich folks like us are exposed to more threats. You can't just blame everything on me, it's unfair.

steps.speaker: Levy
steps.content: Moreover, my nephew... He's so young and innocent. I can't bear watching him misstep and become my cousin's hired gun.

steps.speaker: Levy
steps.content: I mean, Chief, isn't it your hobby to save poor Sinners from their plight? Or does my pitiful nephew not deserve your saving just because he's not a Sinner?
My saving? He's under no death threat.

steps.speaker: Levy
steps.content: Oh, of course, I know Chaddy's life's not in danger. It's only a metaphor.

steps.speaker: Levy
steps.content: But imagine, a young man trapped between his father and his uncle. His father has been teaching and forcing him to shoot his uncle. How will he know how to handle such a messed-up situation?

steps.speaker: Levy
steps.content: Now is probably the darkest moment of his life. He has no one to rely on, no one to listen to him. God knows what kind of despair he's in.

steps.speaker: Levy
steps.content: If I don't visit him and help him sort things out, he may just stray onto the wrong path and end up a scoundrel like me.
So far, we've found no evidence his father may have manipulated him to do it.

steps.speaker: Levy
steps.content: All the more reason to see him then. You won't make any progress if you don't ask him directly.

steps.speaker: Levy
steps.content: If you're that worried, why don't you come with me? Haven't you got the shackles? What can I do with that thing on me?

steps.speaker: Levy
steps.content: Aha, I know you're reasonable.
From what you know about Levy, he wants more than just to cheer his nephew up.
You're not someone who'd waste energy on something that doesn't benefit you... You're manipulative and vengeful, and you don't work for nothing. That's your style.
What can you gain from this?

steps.speaker: Levy
steps.content: Ahaha, you still remember what happened before.

steps.speaker: Levy
steps.content: That was just a game. Using unconventional means to reach your goal in a game isn't illegal, is it?

steps.speaker: Levy
steps.content: Speaking of which, Chief... Don't you think we all live in a game? Since we're already in it, it's only fair that we try to have some fun. Following rules is just too boring.

steps.speaker: Levy
steps.content: Top players are often the ones who've found the loopholes. If you don't get caught, you win everything. If you do, well, you get kicked out. Sounds fair to me.
So reality is just a game to you? Morals and law don't mean anything to you as long as it's fun?

steps.speaker: Levy
steps.content: Oh come on, don't blow it out of proportion. First of all, there are many types of fun. It's fun to watch someone you dislike trip over, just like it's fun to see a loved one happy.

steps.speaker: Levy
steps.content: For example, when I say I want to have a chat with Chaddy, I'm also doing that for fun.
You want to amuse yourself by mocking your nephew?

steps.speaker: Levy
steps.content: Hahaha, that's a reasonable guess. Though it's quite an interesting proposition, that's not what I have in mind.

steps.speaker: Levy
steps.content: I'm going to see him to feed my empathy.

steps.speaker: Levy
steps.content: Does it sound strange to you? That someone like me can have empathy too?

steps.speaker: Levy
steps.content: You have many fearsome Sinners in the MBCC too. Are they all animals without a bit of human nature in them? I suppose not?

steps.speaker: Levy
steps.content: I may not be morally flawless, but surely I'm not worse than a murderer or an arsonist?
As he said that, Levy laughed and turned his gaze away.

steps.speaker: Levy
steps.content: ...I'm probably doing this because Chad reminds me of my young self. Cute and naive, thinking that simply because you care about others, they'll return the favor.

steps.speaker: Levy
steps.content: Sadly, kindness will always be negative equity. Those who still keep their conscience and guilt are doomed to be eaten alive by swindlers.
"Cute and naive" sounds like the polar opposite of you. I thought you were a swindler yourself.

steps.speaker: Levy
steps.content: Let's not dig up the past. I'm a decent businessman in the real world. I have all the normal human emotions, I just tend to focus on having fun.

steps.speaker: Levy
steps.content: Oh? It sure takes a lot to convince you. I might give up if this goes on for another 30 minutes. After all, it doesn't feel very cost-effective to waste so much energy on a nephew who's stepped out of line.
I can give you a chance to visit Chad. But if I notice any improper behavior...

steps.speaker: Levy
steps.content: I know, I know. You've got the almighty shackles. If I really end up selling Chaddy to a private Hypercube mine as a coolie, you'll make me pay for it.

steps.speaker: Levy
steps.content: Stop wasting time here. Let's go.
